title: The Battle Before The Battle
subtitle: When The Leader Cannot Say “I Was Wrong”
tagline: The higher your authority rises, the more expensive your inability to repent becomes for everyone beneath it.
headline: When Leaders Can’t Admit They Were Wrong
headline_sub: Are You More Concerned About Being Right, or Becoming Right?
seo_title: When Leaders Can’t Admit They Were Wrong | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Leaders who can’t say “I was wrong” make everyone beneath them pay. A biblical look at Saul, David and owning mistakes at work, on teams and at home.
og_image_alt: When Leaders Can’t Admit They Were Wrong: The higher your authority rises, the more expensive your inability to repent becomes for everyone beneath it. TheWrkShop, Leadership & Culture.

scriptures.text: Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.”
Saul replied, “I have sinned. But please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel….”

blocks.text: “But please honor me before the elders….”
David, confronted by Nathan after grievous sin, says:

items: Repentance does not erase its consequences.

blocks.text: But David gives us something Saul repeatedly struggled to give:

items: This isn’t a comparison declaring David’s failures small.

blocks.text: It exposes two different responses to being revealed.
REPENTANCE DOES NOT WEAKEN HEALTHY AUTHORITY.
REPENTANCE IS PART OF CHRISTIAN LEADERSHIP.
Everyone else must begin carrying the leader’s version of reality.

items: So someone else must absorb blame.

blocks.text: EVERYONE MUST PROTECT THE LEADER FROM THE TRUTH ABOUT THE LEADER.

items: WHEN WAS THE LAST TIME I APOLOGIZED TO SOMEONE I LEAD?
CAN I NAME A RECENT DECISION I GOT WRONG?
DO I EXPLAIN BEFORE I OWN?
AM I MORE CONCERNED ABOUT BEING RIGHT OR BECOMING RIGHT?

blocks.text: WHAT DOES MY REPENTANCE TEACH THE ROOM?
There may be someone who needs five words from you:
The higher your authority rises, the more expensive your inability to repent becomes for everyone beneath it.

items: Destroy the pride that makes confession feel threatening.
Give me courage to own what belongs to me.
Keep me from protecting reputation at the expense of truth.

blocks.text: Make my repentance part of how I lead.
The higher your authority rises, the more expensive your inability to repent becomes for everyone beneath it.
“The leader is never wrong” isn’t strength. It’s fragility with authority.
Repentance is part of Christian leadership.
Everyone should not have to protect the leader from the truth about the leader.
Am I more concerned about being right, or becoming right?
